text:
maria: heads up — saw a spike in provisional token charges for a customer today after we routed them to the small-fallback model during a streaming reconnect. looks like client rejoined, we resumed the stream, sent a truncated toolcall, then final commit to the big model — but provisional ledger kept the small-model tokens.

alex: ugh, seen that pattern before. do you have a log snippet + request ids? might be the resume path not marking the provisional as superseded when the final commit arrives.

maria: pasted snippets below (redacted ids). logs show resume session, toolcall TTL expired, then fallback route. note the accounting events: provisional_increment -> resume_chunk -> final_commit but ledger never refunded provisional.

maria: ```
[I] 2026-03-20T14:02:11Z session=sess_7f resume chunk=123 prefix_len=42 provisional_tokens=18
[I] 2026-03-20T14:02:13Z route=small-fallback model=redwood-small toolcall_id=tc_9 ttl_ms=45000 truncated=true provisional_increment=18
[I] 2026-03-20T14:02:17Z route=primary model=redwood-larger final_commit=true committed_tokens=54
[I] 2026-03-20T14:02:18Z billing=noop provisional_locked=18
```

sarah: that `billing=noop provisional_locked` line is the symptom. looks like our provisional->commit reconcile job only handles cases where final_commit references the same provisional token id. on resume the provisional token id changes (we generate new provisional ids for each resume).

alex: can we change resume to carry a stable session_provisional_id that persists across reconnects? then commit can reference it and the reconcile becomes simple. downside: harder to correlate partial prefixes across route switches.

maria: agree stable id would help. alternate thought: make commit events include a list of provisional_ids they cover (so commit can claim multiple provisional segments). then reconcile would mark them settled. aware that increases event size but keeps idempotency.

infra-bot: FYI, rollout risk analysis for either change: persistent provisional_id requires a migration to ledger schema (add nullable field session_provisional_id). Larger commit payload impacts kafka message size under high-throughput streaming. Both require console changes to surface these mappings.

mike: another edge: toolcalls that get truncated mid-stream create partial charges attributed to toolcall boundaries. if the toolcall is retried on final model, we double-charge provisional unless we dedupe by `toolcall_nonce` + `session_uuid`. maybe we should enforce a canonical id for toolcall attempts.

liz: from console/product POV: customers get very confused when they see provisional charges and then nothing in committed. we need a small UX bandage: in the route trace show provisional buckets with hover text "provisional — pending commit or refund" and an action to request manual reconciliation for a window. also show fallback history so they can see model switches.

alex: okay practical proposal: 1) add session_provisional_id that persists for stream session across reconnects, 2) include commit_provisional_refs: [id...] in final commit event to allow multi-segment reconciliation, 3) emit telemetry metric `provisional_unsettled_count_by_route` for dashboard alerts. rollout plan: feature-flag ledger schema change + kafka consumer tolerant to missing field.

maria: any objections on approach? ordering: small migration -> API change to include refs -> console tweaks. flagged for canary on dedicated customers only first.

sarah: couple more gotchas — when we fallback to a smaller model we sometimes truncate tokens/client side (client may drop suffix). that means the final committed token count can be less than provisional sum; need refund path to adjust ledger and emit a `provisional_refunded` event with reason `truncation_on_fallback` + short audit string.

mike: incrementally, we could also add a short TTL for provisional entries (e.g. 2m) after which they auto-expire and reconcile as refunded if no commit arrives — but must be careful for long-lived streams. maybe make TTL configurable per plan.

liz: yeah TTL per plan is fine. also add console filter: show provisional-only for last X hours. customers will want to see why charges changed after a day.

alex: ok i'll draft the PR for schema + API changes. maria can you attach one more real example and the customer id so we can repro in staging? i'll try to wire `commit_provisional_refs` into the router so final commit references the active provisional ids.

maria: will do. for repro steps: start stream, force fallback by simulating capacity pressure, truncate toolcall on small model, then reconnect to primary. i'll drop steps + customer id in the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created ticket INF-1219 for ledger migration / provisional-id change (owner alex).
